data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -x

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --output=run.out
#   --error=run.err
#   --time=00:30:00
#   --partition=batch

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 4 \
  --time=30m \
  --queue=batch \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm --output/--error via redirection.
exec >run.out 2>run.err

export LD_PRELOAD=$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_def.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_avx2.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_lp64.so:$EBROOTIMKL/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_thread.so:$EBROOTIMKL/lib/intel64/libiomp5.so

export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/p/project/ccstma/cstma000/pySDC

# Slurm used srun; within Flux we run directly inside the allocation.
# Performance implication: if this should run as multiple ranks, invoking plain python may only run one process.
python pySDC_with_PETSc.py 1

touch ready
'
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
